evidence.source: docs/decisions.md on the story branch; docs/debates/context-api/debate.md

P1.text: API: `$getContext(C)` reads the nearest provider and throws without one, as today. `$getContext(C, fallback)` returns the provided value, or `fallback` when no provider is above. Whether a fallback was given is decided by the argument count at compile time, as Vue's arguments.length, so `$getContext(C, undefined)` is the optional read. Types: `$getContext<T>(c: Context<T>): T` and `$getContext<T, F>(c: Context<T>, fallback: F): T | F`. A provided undefined is a value (presence is `key in v`, J2).

evidence.detail: Qwik and Vue shape; Vue's presence rule

P2.text: The fallback is an expression evaluated in the reader's scope, only when no provider is found (like `??`), once per read. Nothing is stored on the context, so no value is shared across requests. A module value passed as a fallback is the app's own choice, as with any import.

evidence.detail: the leak came from a value stored on the context object

P3.text: Runtime: one walk per read. The compiled guarded read `has(C, scope) ? consume(C, scope) : undefined` becomes `consume(C, scope, fallback)` on the server and in the browser, with the fallback compiled as a function only when it is not a literal. `has()` and `hasContext()` are deleted.

evidence.detail: guarded reads compile to has ? consume : undefined

P4.text: `$hasContext` is removed. The 2 standalone reads become `$getContext(ToolbarContext, false)`, which is the boolean they want. A context is then read one way.

P5.text: $store stays store only. A store in an optional context is read with a guard on the value: `const g = $getContext(C, undefined); const s = g ? $store(g.state) : undefined;`. The compiler accepts that one guarded form for a const g read with a fallback (the guard is fixed since contexts are static) and reports any other as BRM197 with the new form in its message.

evidence.detail: the guard machinery moves from $hasContext to the fallback read

P6.text: Work: node store-only-source is rewritten as context-read-fallback (L): compiler, runtime, types, BRM197 text, tests, docs and decisions.md, plus a scripted rewrite of the about 140 guarded and 63 g?.state ui readers. Split the ui rewrite into its own M node only if the core node's diff passes 60 files.
